format:
  revealjs:
    footer: "UAV Design — Lecture 1"
    css: styles.css
    include-after-body:
      text: |
        <script>
        (function () {
          // The UAV taxonomy slide (see the `.taxonomy-slide` section below)
          // embeds a full page, not slide content, so it should look like
          // the browser tab it would be if you opened that page directly:
          // no reveal.js margin gutter, footer, or slide number around it.
          // reveal.js scales the whole deck with a CSS transform on
          // `.reveal .slides`, and any transformed ancestor becomes the
          // containing block for `position: fixed` descendants (a real CSS
          // gotcha, confirmed by inspecting computed styles) — so a fixed,
          // 100vw/100vh overlay placed *inside* the deck would inherit that
          // transform and render offset/scaled instead of covering the true
          // viewport. This block runs from `include-after-body`, which
          // Quarto places as a sibling *after* the whole `.reveal` div, so
          // the overlay iframe it creates sits outside that transformed
          // ancestor chain and can genuinely cover the full browser window.
          var slideIframe = document.querySelector('.taxonomy-wrap iframe');
          if (!slideIframe || !window.Reveal) return;

          var overlay = document.createElement('iframe');
          overlay.id = 'taxonomy-fullpage-overlay';
          overlay.src = slideIframe.getAttribute('src');
          overlay.title = slideIframe.getAttribute('title');
          document.body.appendChild(overlay);

          // The overlay covers the whole window and steals keyboard focus
          // once you click into it, so reveal's own arrow-key/click
          // navigation can't reach the deck underneath — these two buttons
          // are the only way to change slides while it's showing.
          function makeNavButton(id, label, glyph, action) {
            var btn = document.createElement('button');
            btn.id = id;
            btn.type = 'button';
            btn.className = 'taxonomy-nav-btn';
            btn.setAttribute('aria-label', label);
            btn.textContent = glyph;
            btn.addEventListener('click', action);
            document.body.appendChild(btn);
            return btn;
          }
          var prevBtn = makeNavButton('taxonomy-nav-prev', 'Previous slide', '‹', function () { Reveal.prev(); });
          var nextBtn = makeNavButton('taxonomy-nav-next', 'Next slide', '›', function () { Reveal.next(); });

          function syncOverlay() {
            var current = Reveal.getCurrentSlide();
            var shown = current && current.classList.contains('taxonomy-slide') ? 'block' : 'none';
            overlay.style.display = shown;
            prevBtn.style.display = shown;
            nextBtn.style.display = shown;
          }
          Reveal.on('ready', syncOverlay);
          Reveal.on('slidechanged', syncOverlay);
        })();
        </script>

## Zipline Platform 1

::: {.video-wrap}
<iframe data-external="1" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/jEbRVNxL44c" title="Zipline Rewanda Opperations and Vehicle Design" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope" allowfullscreen></iframe>

## Zipline Platform 1 Body {.frame-wrap-slide}

::: {.frame-wrap style="--frame-width: 95%;"}
![](media/zipline_body.png){.frame-img}

::: {.frame-overlay}
[]{.fragment .circle style="top: 5%; left: 40%; width: 12%; height: 35%; --shape-color: rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.85);"}
[**Two Rotors** — The front rotor is always on but the rear rotor turns off and folds up during cruise.]{.fragment .callout style="top: 8%; left: 2%; --callout-line-color: rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.85);"}

[**Materials** — Everything is a low cost material on the airframe.]{.fragment .callout style="top: 62%; right: 2%; left: auto; text-align: right; --callout-line-color: rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.85);"}
:::
:::

## Zipline Platform 1 Modular Components {.frame-row-slide}

::: {.frame-row style="--frame-width: 95%;"}
::: {.frame-col style="--img-shift-x: 0%; --img-shift-y: 0%;"}
![](media/zipline_battery.png)

::: {.frame-overlay}
[**GPS Embedded in Battery** — The GPS is never powered down because it is always attached to the battery decreasing the change of a slow cold start.]{.fragment .callout style="top: 8%; left: 2%; max-width: 45%; font-size: 0.7em; --callout-line-color: rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.85);"}
:::
:::

::: {.frame-col}
![](media/zipline_wings.png)
:::

::: {.footer}
The battery and wings are completely modular so that the wings can be easily replaced and that the batteries can be charged and cycled indepent of the body, decreasing turn around time.
:::
:::

## Zipline Platform 1 Launcher {.frame-wrap-slide}

::: {.frame-wrap style="--frame-width: 95%;"}
![](media/zipline_launcher.png){.frame-img}


::: {.footer}
The launcher allows for smaller rotors and thrust reducing the aircraft weight while also decreasing the footprint needed removing the need for a runway.
:::
:::

## Zipline Platform 1 Capture {.frame-row-slide}

::: {.frame-row style="--frame-width: 95%;"}
::: {.frame-col style="--img-shift-x: -50%; --img-shift-y: -20%;"}
![](media/zipline_capture.png)
:::

::: {.frame-col}
![](media/zipline_tailhook.png)
:::

::: {.footer}
The capture uses a hook on the tail of the UAV to hook the aircraft with a rope removing the need for landing gear on the UAV and decreasing the landing related damage. 
:::
